title: Security review - Data residency & region pinning
next_steps: Send SOC 2 + ISO27001 certificates and policy pack (Ava)
Schedule technical deep dive on KMS/BYOK and on-prem options (Priya/Daniel) - target 2027-04-15
Provide sub-processor list and DPIA summary (Ava)
Follow up with pilot contract terms and pricing (Ava)
action_items: Ava Martinez: Send security package (SOC2, ISO) by 2027-04-09
Daniel Cho: Region-pinning architecture diagram and notes by 2027-04-12
CardioHealth - Priya Nair: Confirm compliance stakeholders and availability for deep dive by 2027-04-11
summary: High-level security review focused on data residency, region pinning, cross-border processing, and KMS/BYOK options. CardioHealth wants EU-only processing for patient data and full audit logs; evaluating Hosted + VPC vs Private deployment. Redwood team to share certs, region-pinning design, and schedule deeper technical session.
questions: Can Redwood guarantee data stays in EU region for processing and storage?
How does Redwood handle KV/prefix cache and cross-region fallbacks?
What sub-processors are involved in hosted + dedicated?
Is BYOK/HSM available for private and hosted?
Audit log retention and export options?
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-04-08 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood Solutions), Lena Fischer (CISO, CardioHealth), Marco Santini (VP Eng), Priya Nair (Lead Cloud Architect), Omar Reyes (Legal)

Auto-generated summary: CardioHealth requires EU-only processing for PHI, wants clarity on region pinning, sub-processors, and KMS/BYOK. Redwood to provide security pack and run a tech deep dive focused on key management and private deployment options.

00:00 - Ava Martinez: Hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick round robin, then we'll jump into the data residency items.
00:18 - Lena Fischer: Hi, Lena here — CISO at CardioHealth. we're mostly focused on patient data residency and audit trails, so uh we'll be asking a lot about region pinning and sub-processors.
00:30 - Marco Santini: Marco here, VP Eng. looking at integration complexity and latency tradeoffs.
00:38 - Priya Nair: Priya - cloud architect. we need to understand KMS/BYOK options.
00:45 - Ava Martinez: Great. Daniel from our infra team will walk through architecture.
01:05 - Daniel Cho: Yep, hi all. quick disclaimer, I'll jump between high-level and some implementation notes. At a high level, Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private. For EU-only processing we generally recommend either (a) hosted with strict region-pinning and contractual commitments and sub-processor restrictions, or (b) Private (VPC/on-prem) for the strictest control.
01:40 - Priya Nair: can you guarantee processing stays in eu? like, no cross-border tokenization or temporary caching in us?
01:50 - Daniel Cho: short answer: yes we can pin requests to an EU region and avoid cross-region compute, but there are nuances. for hosted mode we offer region pinning at the customer tenancy level — routing policies send requests to EU clusters only. However, certain control plane operations (metering, billing) may touch us-based services unless contractual terms exclude that; so we add contractual data processing clauses and put limitations in the DPA.
02:25 - Lena Fischer: that's a key point — billing/metrics touching us is okay as long as no PHI leaves eu. what about logs and KV cache?
02:34 - Daniel Cho: right. the inference data path — model input/output, KV cache — can be configured to stay in eu clusters. note: caching layers sometimes have metadata replicated for availability; we can disable cross-region replication for your tenancy. there's a small availability tradeoff if we remove replication, but you avoid cross-border copies.
03:05 - Marco Santini: any chance of transient fallbacks to us nodes if eu capacity is exhausted? we've seen other vendors do that and it's a dealbreaker for us.
03:18 - Ava Martinez: good callout. our standard policy for enterprise EU-pinned customers is no cross-border fallback by default; we can enable controlled fallback with explicit permission and audit hooks, but for CardioHealth we'd recommend disabling fallback.
03:36 - Priya Nair: how do you prove that? we've got auditors that will want logs and provenance.
03:45 - Daniel Cho: we provide detailed audit logs with region tags and request IDs. logs include processing region, cluster id, and model variant. we also can produce an artefact for audits: per-request provenance for a sample set or for all requests depending on retention. export is via S3-compatible export or direct syslog to your tenant.
04:12 - Omar Reyes: legal here — the DPIA and sub-processor list is important. who are the sub-processors for hosted and for Dedicated?
04:22 - Ava Martinez: our sub-processor list includes major cloud infra providers for hosted (we'll send the up-to-date list), telemetry vendors for analytics, and some managed service partners. for Dedicated and Private, the sub-processor surface is much smaller — if you're on Private on-prem there are effectively no third-party infra sub-processors. we'll share the list and the sub-processor contracts.
04:48 - Lena Fischer: okay. is there any on-the-fly translation or preprocessing that might leak content to third parties? e.g., if you use third-party embeddings or moderation?
04:58 - Daniel Cho: great question. for CardioHealth we recommend disabling any optional third-party enrichment. Redwood's default hosted offering can integrate third-party ops for things like anonymization if customers opt in; we will not enable that without signoff. all enrichment steps are controlled in the data flow and we can guarantee no third-party calls for your tenancy.
05:30 - Marco Santini: walk me through encryption — at rest and in transit. BYOK? HSM?
05:38 - Daniel Cho: data in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. at rest we encrypt with AES-256. for hosted and dedicated we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations; keys can be in EU regions with supported HSM providers. For Private we support direct HSM integration on-prem. Note: some operational metadata (billing metrics) may still be encrypted under Redwood-managed keys unless specified in contract.
06:05 - Priya Nair: important for us that KMS keys never leave eu and that key control is with us. is BYOK full scope? like, can we revoke keys and ensure data can't be decrypted?
06:18 - Daniel Cho: yes. BYOK works such that revoking the key will prevent decryption of newly-read data. we also offer a key-rotation path and key escrow options for long-term retention requirements. we'll attach a diagram to show key lifecycle.
06:40 - Lena Fischer: audit logs retention — what's default and options? we need at least 7 years for certain records.
06:48 - Ava Martinez: default retention is 90 days in the console; enterprise packages offer extended retention to your retention policy (customizable, S3 export to your bucket for long-term archival). we can configure log forwarders so you get immutable storage in eu.
07:10 - Marco Santini: how about RBAC/SSO? we need SCIM + SAML with role-based controls scoped to environments.
07:19 - Daniel Cho: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, plus fine-grained RBAC. roles can be limited to eu-tenancy resources. we have audit trails for admin actions and token usage.
07:40 - Priya Nair: what about model artifacts — do you keep copies of fine-tuned models or artifacts that could contain PHI?
07:48 - Daniel Cho: we store model artifacts per tenancy; for hosted, we keep versions used in production. we can configure policy to not persist fine-tuned customer-trained models on shared storage or to isolate them in your dedicated storage. again, Private eliminates shared persistence.
08:10 - Lena Fischer: any SOC 2 / ISO certs?
08:15 - Ava Martinez: yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. we'll attach the certs and the executive summary in the security package.
08:25 - Omar Reyes: regarding cross-border legal basis — do you have standard DPA clauses that ensure EU data subject protections?
08:32 - Ava Martinez: yes, our DPA includes EU SCCs where applicable and we can add contractual clauses to limit processing locations. we'll share our DPA redline.
09:10 - Marco Santini: performance/latency tradeoffs — if we disable replication for EU-only, what's impact on latency?
09:20 - Daniel Cho: replication mostly affects availability and cold-starts for KV cache. disabling cross-region replication may add a bit more cold-start latency for rare requests if EU nodes must load KV; steady-state latency is unaffected. We'll share benchmarks showing p50/p95 with replication disabled vs enabled.
09:48 - Lena Fischer: are any of your sub-processors outside eu? we need to know for DPIA.
09:54 - Ava Martinez: some telemetry and analytics vendors are US-based — we can provide options to opt out or to use EU-based alternatives.
10:10 - Priya Nair: the other concern is embeddings and downstream storage — if we index patient text into embeddings, where do vectors live?
10:18 - Daniel Cho: embeddings are stored in your tenancy's region. we support EU-only vector stores. for hosted, if you request eu pinning, they never leave eu. we do offer managed vector DB partners, but for strict EU needs we recommend either dedicated or private vector storage in eu.
10:45 - Marco Santini: can you give an example of a per-request provenance log?
10:52 - Daniel Cho: sure. sample entry: timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, processing_region, cluster_id, model_id, model_version, topology (dedicated/shared), and KMS-key-id. We'll redact or anonymize content but maintain metadata.
11:20 - Lena Fischer: retention of that provenance — can it be put into our S3 for the 7-year requirement?
11:27 - Daniel Cho: yes, we support direct export to your S3 bucket (eu region) with lifecycle rules you control.
12:00 - Ava Martinez: quick pause — any compliance red flags so far?
12:06 - Lena Fischer: still worried about the control plane touching non-EU services. need concrete contract language.
12:12 - Ava Martinez: understood, we'll include explicit clauses in DPA and show a scope diagram of control-plane interactions.
12:35 - Marco Santini: are there monitoring agents or collectors that phone home?
12:40 - Daniel Cho: minimal telemetry for telemetry health but for enterprise we can disable or direct those telemetry streams to your collectors; we also offer on-prem collectors in private deployments.
13:05 - Priya Nair: what's the upgrade/fallback story for critical patches if we are private on-prem? can you push patches?
13:15 - Maya Patel: for on-prem/private we can do scheduled upgrades via your deployment pipelines or manage it under a managed-services agreement — patches are tested in staging and applied with your ops team.
13:40 - Marco Santini: about data subject requests — do you have tooling to find and delete a specific customer's records?
13:48 - Daniel Cho: yes. we have a deletion API and can run targeted purge jobs. For embeddings this means removing vectors and any cached tokens; we'll provide a runbook for data subject requests.
14:15 - Lena Fischer: any known incidents where data left region?
14:20 - Ava Martinez: No region-exfil incidents. we do record any cross-border processes in our change log and can show previous audit reports.
14:38 - Omar Reyes: what about subprocessors in support — do support engineers tunnel into instances that may be in eu?
14:46 - Daniel Cho: support access is role-limited and audited. for eu-pinned tenancies we can restrict support access to eu-only bastions and require jumpbox audit and session recording.
15:05 - Marco Santini: ok, let's talk about legal obligations for sub-processor changes — how are we notified?
15:11 - Ava Martinez: we provide 30 days' notice for sub-processor changes for enterprise customers and immediate notice for critical changes. we also allow contractual veto for certain categories.
15:35 - Priya Nair: what's the model routing if we autmatically fallback to cheaper variant? might that change region?
15:44 - Daniel Cho: model routing is per-policy; for CardioHealth we would pin both routing and model variants to eu-only variants. auto-fallback across regions is disabled unless you opt in.
16:08 - Marco Santini: can you share a network diagram? specifically any egress paths to non-eu endpoints?
16:14 - Ava Martinez: yes — Daniel will attach the region-pinning diagram and control plane interactions.
16:30 - Daniel Cho: just to be explicit: for hosted EU tenancy we run compute, storage, and KV in EU clusters. control plane metadata/operational metrics may traverse other regions but we can contractually limit the data that goes cross-border.
17:00 - Lena Fischer: backups? cross-border backup replication?
17:06 - Daniel Cho: backups are region-local by default for EU tenancies; cross-region backup is opt-in for DR and requires explicit consent.
17:28 - Priya Nair: regulatory third-party audits — can we get penetration test reports?
17:33 - Ava Martinez: we can provide summaries and high-level results; for detailed pentest reports we typically have an NDA process — we'll start that if you want the full report.
17:55 - Marco Santini: thinking about availability — if we disable replication, what's our RTO/RPO?
18:02 - Daniel Cho: without cross-region replication, RPO is bounded by single-region durability SLA; typical RTO is within your Dedicated SLA (we'll provide numbers), Private is dependent on your infra. We'll add a table in the follow-up doc.
18:30 - Ava Martinez: quick check — Priya, would you prefer a hosted EU-pinned tenancy first or go straight to Dedicated/Private?
18:40 - Priya Nair: we'd like to try hosted EU-pinned for evaluation if you can meet contractual restrictions and guarantee no cross-border fallbacks. If not, we'll consider Dedicated.
18:55 - Daniel Cho: that's reasonable. for the pilot we can provision an EU-only hosted tenancy with fallbacks disabled, BYOK enabled, and log export to your S3.
19:10 - Lena Fischer: pilot scope — how many queries, sample PII handling, audit sampling?
19:18 - Ava Martinez: recommend starting with non-production traffic and a sample of PHI to validate. we'll define scope in the pilot doc.
19:35 - Marco Santini: one more: are any open-source components that have external telemetry?
19:42 - Daniel Cho: some OSS libs phone home for updates if enabled; we keep them disabled by default in enterprise builds and can audit third-party libs.
20:00 - Omar Reyes: contractual SLAs — can you include region-specific SLOs?
20:06 - Ava Martinez: yes, SLOs can be region-bound in Dedicated contracts; for hosted we provide p95 latencies per region in the SLA addendum.
20:25 - Priya Nair: ok. can we also have a list of data elements that Redwood considers "system metadata" vs "customer data"? that's part of our DPIA.
20:34 - Daniel Cho: yes, we'll include a glossary in the packet. system metadata includes telemetry and usage metrics, customer data is model inputs/outputs and persisted artifacts.
21:00 - Marco Santini: what's your incident response for a suspected cross-border leak?
21:06 - Ava Martinez: immediate containment, forensics, customer notification within the timeframe in our incident policy; we'll share the runbook.
21:30 - Priya Nair: ok good. anything about EU data subject rights where the processor must assist controllers?
21:37 - Daniel Cho: yes, we have a controller/processor playbook and support for SARs with APIs and operational runbooks.
22:00 - Lena Fischer: thanks. can you confirm the export mechanism for audit logs?
22:06 - Daniel Cho: yes — S3 export (eu), syslog, and direct streaming to your SIEM via webhook.
22:30 - Maya Patel: we'll include sample commands and a walkthrough in the follow-up.
23:00 - Marco Santini: can you show cost delta for BYOK + EU-only tenancy vs default?
23:08 - Ava Martinez: we'll provide a cost sheet. there's a small premium for dedicated key management and single-region isolation.
23:40 - Priya Nair: anything around employee access controls and background checks for engineers who may access eu clusters?
23:48 - Ava Martinez: employees with access are background checked; we can provide more details in HR security questionnaire. we also have RBAC and session recording for access to production.
24:12 - Lena Fischer: ok, next steps?
24:18 - Ava Martinez: recap: we'll share SOC2/ISO certs, DPA redline, sub-processor list, region-pinning diagram, and schedule technical deep dive the week of 2027-04-15. pilot provisioning if CardioHealth agrees.
24:35 - Priya Nair: please include a clear statement in the packet that cross-border fallback is disabled for the pilot.
24:44 - Daniel Cho: noted; will include config flags and auditable settings.
25:00 - Omar Reyes: legal will review DPA. please tag any clauses related to control plane telemetry.
25:08 - Ava Martinez: will do.
25:20 - [General discussion continues — details about pilot scope, duration, roles — redacted for brevity]
38:10 - Daniel Cho: technical note — KV cache behavior: we shard cache per region and do not cross replicate for EU tenancy. there is an internal optimization that occasionally creates metadata fingerprints that we can disable.
40:00 - Marco Santini: thanks. important that the internal optimization be disabled.
40:05 - Daniel Cho: understood.
44:50 - Lena Fischer: final question — if we later want to add on-prem for certain workflows, how disruptive is migration?
44:58 - Daniel Cho: migration path is supported; we keep artifacts exportable and can do a staged cutover. we'll outline steps.
46:20 - Ava Martinez: ok let's close with explicit next steps and owners — we'll put everything in the follow-up email.
46:30 - Priya Nair: thanks everyone.
46:35 - Marco Santini: thanks.
46:40 - Lena Fischer: appreciate it.
51:30 - Call ends.

End summary: Redwood to provide security package, region-pinning diagrams, sub-processor list, and schedule deep technical session. CardioHealth to confirm pilot scope and internal stakeholders.
